steps: Mix the jowar flour, besan and atta with the onion, coriander leaves, green chilli, turmeric, chilli and coriander powders, cumin and salt.
Add about 40 to 50 ml water a person, a little at a time, and knead into a soft, moist, smooth dough.
Heat a tawa on medium-high heat and brush it with a little oil.
Pat a ball of dough flat on a wet cloth or oiled sheet, about 5 mm thick, and poke 3 or 4 holes in it.
Flip it onto the hot tawa, peel off the cloth, and drop a little oil into the holes and round the edge.
Cover and cook on medium for 2 to 3 minutes, until the base is golden and crisp.
Turn it over and cook the other side until it has brown spots.
Serve hot with a little butter on top.
note: This is the quick weeknight version with three flours instead of a roasted bhajani mix; bajra, rice flour and sesame are left out to keep the shopping short. 60 g of flour makes about three small thalipeeth a plate.
